subject: How to not save predictions calculated for DIC (and maybe WAIC)

messages.author: 23a345c7bcfdb75b
messages.subject: How to not save predictions calculated for DIC (and maybe WAIC)
parts:
Dear all,

In all my models fitted with Stan, I include a generated quantities block in order to get what is needed to later calculate DIC and WAIC. Hoever, in my current model, I am trying a slight modification since the matrix with the predicted values is consuming too much memory due to the data and model having respectively N~200k and iter~100k. Therefore, I want to get the predicted values to at least calculate DIC and them discard them (I don't know if WAIC will be possible to get).

Let me explain it better. Suppose I have something like, for instance, the following:

generated quantities{
  vector[N] p;
  real log_lik;
  log_lik <- 0;
  for ( i in 1:N ) {
    p[i] <- b_0 + X[i]*b_1;
  }
  log_lik <- bernoulli_logit_log( win , p );
  dev <- dev + (-2)*log_lik
}

In my situation, just saving the sampling of vector 'p' results in a 200k x 100k matrix, what is of course draining the RAM memory, the hardware memory and even delaying the processing of the model run. Therefore, what I would like to know first is:

1)  whether there is an efficient way for me to retrieve only 'log_lik' and 'dev' (in the example above, not saving 'p'). If my model had few parameters, I though that one solution for RStan users like myself could be to pass the name of all parameters but 'p' in the "pars" option of the "stan" function. But my model is a multilevel model, in which I end up having more than two hundred parameters. It doesn't seem to make sense to inform all the hundreds of parameters names, just leaving 'p' out. I hope there is a better way of achieving that. Maybe a direct way within the Stan model itself?

Second thing is:

2) by the code above, what I've called log_lik is not exactly the same as in the discussion of the BDA3 and in Gelman and Vehtari, 2015, since I am saving only one value of log_lik per iteration, not the full log_lik matrix of dimensions n x iter. Would it be still reasonable to calculate WAIC with he resultant log_lik, even if less ideal?

Thanks for your time!

Fabricio Vasselai
Polisci Dep. - USP



PS: maybe a future feature for the "stan" function in RStan would be to have "pars_keep" and "pars_drop" options, instead of only "pars".  Then, one could both specify parameters to be kept but also parameters to be dropped.

On Thursday, July 16, 2015 at 1:46:29 AM UTC-4, Fabricio Vasselai wrote:
Let me explain it better. Suppose I have something like, for instance, the following:

generated quantities{
  vector[N] p;
  real log_lik;
  log_lik <- 0;
  for ( i in 1:N ) {
    p[i] <- b_0 + X[i]*b_1;
  }
  log_lik <- bernoulli_logit_log( win , p );
  dev <- dev + (-2)*log_lik
}

In my situation, just saving the sampling of vector 'p' results in a 200k x 100k matrix, what is of course draining the RAM memory, the hardware memory and even delaying the processing of the model run. Therefore, what I would like to know first is:

1)  whether there is an efficient way for me to retrieve only 'log_lik' and 'dev' (in the example above, not saving 'p').

Yes, like this (you need to declare dev)

generated quantities {
  real log_lik;
  real dev;
  log_lik <- 0;
  dev <- 0;
  {
    vector[N] p;

for ( i in 1:N ) p[i] <- b_0 + X[i]*b_1;
    log_lik <- bernoulli_logit_log( win , p );
    dev <- dev + (-2)*log_lik
  }
}
Second thing is:

2) by the code above, what I've called log_lik is not exactly the same as in the discussion of the BDA3 and in Gelman and Vehtari, 2015, since I am saving only one value of log_lik per iteration, not the full log_lik matrix of dimensions n x iter. Would it be still reasonable to calculate WAIC with he resultant log_lik, even if less ideal?
No.

PS: maybe a future feature for the "stan" function in RStan would be to have "pars_keep" and "pars_drop" options, instead of only "pars".  Then, one could both specify parameters to be kept but also parameters to be dropped.

We've implemented that option for months but not released it. You still specify pars = "p" but add include = FALSE to exclude p.

Ben

parts:
Many thanks for the prompt replies.

Quick reactions:
| For reasons discussed in our paper with Hwang, we prefer LOO or WAIC to DIC.

Sure thing, I read it, agreed and now am onboard the WAIC ship. However, as mentioned, it's become hard for me to generate the proper log_lik to calculate WAIC due to the fact that my SxN matrix gets too big, too memory consuming. For the DIC, I can save just the "dev", which is a vector Sx1.
I would love to get the WAIC instead, that's why I asked if my way to generate the log_lik would be enough as an approximation, since it took much less memory. But even before Ben's reply, I was already guessing it would not, since it flattened the log_lik to a point-estimate pattern, thus losing the very best property of the WAIC over the DIC....

| Yes, like this (you need to declare dev)

generated quantities { 
  real log_lik;
  real dev;
  log_lik <- 0;
  dev <- 0;
  {
    vector[N] p;
    for ( i in 1:N ) p[i] <- b_0 + X[i]*b_1;
    log_lik <- bernoulli_logit_log( win , p );
    dev <- dev + (-2)*log_lik
  }
}

Hah, I often forget to declare variables. Glad it was only at the piece of code I wrote here.
Anyways, thanks for the piece of code. That's an elegant within-Stan way of addressing the bulk of my question.
| We've implemented that option for months but not released it. You still specify pars = "p" but add include = FALSE to exclude p.

I'm pretty sure plenty of us will rejoice to see such an option released. I'll stay tuned.

Thanks again.

Fabricio
